headline: Every bottle checked as it leaves the moulder.
label: #e3e7e1
heroLede: BEV Plastics started in 2003 making injection and blow moulds, now runs its own moulding service in Braeside, and has held ISO 9001 certification since 2009. Short shots, flash and warped walls are easy to miss when bottles drop off the machine all shift. This is what a camera check could look like at the outfeed of a blow moulder, shown here with a bottle. The same check works on containers and other moulded parts. Scroll through, then adjust the estimate at the end to your own numbers.
lidLede: The camera checks the neck of every bottle as it leaves the machine: a full, round finish with no flash and no short shot. A bad neck finish is the fault your customer finds when the cap will not seal on their filler.
labelLede: Warped walls, thin spots, blemishes and the wrong colour after a resin change are easy to miss at the outfeed. The camera compares every bottle with good examples your QC team supplies.
codeLede: Where your moulds carry cavity numbers and date inserts, the system reads them on every bottle, so a date insert left unchanged or one faulty cavity shows up straight away.
objectLede: Flash trimmings, regrind and loose parts can end up on the outfeed conveyor. The camera spots anything that should not be there before bottles are bagged or boxed.

vocab.alert: Four short shots in fifteen minutes on Machine 1. Check the parison.
vocab.wrongCode: Date insert not changed: 25 moulded, 26 expected
